title: Your program and the memory map
watch: Watch the `package main` globals box hold `global`, while `local` gets its own slot in the stack frame for `main`.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

var global = 8

func main() {
    local := 3
    fmt.Println(global, local)
}

title: Variables
watch: Watch `main`'s frame: the inner block adds a second `x` slot, and the first `x` still holds 10 after the block ends.

title: Types, sizes and numbers
watch: Watch the value in `n`'s slot jump from 127 straight to -128 on the `n++` step.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    var n int8 = 127
    n++
    fmt.Println(n, 7/2)
}

title: Constants
watch: Watch `red`, `green` and `blue` appear in the `package main` globals box with their values already set before `main` runs a line.

title: Control flow
watch: Watch `i` and `sum` in `main`'s frame; on the turn where `i` is 2, `sum` does not change.

title: Functions and the call stack
watch: Watch a `change` frame stack on top of `main` with its own copy of `x`, then disappear when it returns.

title: Pointers
watch: Watch the arrow from `p` to `x`, then see `x`'s own slot change when `*p = 42` runs.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    x := 10
    p := &x
    *p = 42
    fmt.Println(x)
}

title: Arrays and structs: layout
watch: Watch `a` and `b` each get their own struct object with their own fields; neither one points at the other.

title: Strings
watch: Watch the loop index `i` jump from 1 to 3 as `range` steps over the two-byte `é`.

title: Slices
watch: Watch the arrows from `a` and `b` lead to the same array on the heap, then see its first cell change to 99.

title: Append and growth
watch: Watch whether `b`'s arrow lands in the same heap array as `a` after `append`, or on a new one.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    a := make([]int, 2, 3)
    b := append(a, 7)
    b[0] = 9
    fmt.Println(a, b, cap(b))
}

title: Maps
watch: Watch the map object on the heap: only `count` is stored inside it, yet reading `other` still gives 0.

title: Copy or share?
watch: Watch the arrows from `s` and `t`: both lead to `a`'s array, while `b` is a separate copy with no arrow to `a`.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    a := [2]int{1, 2}; b := a; b[0] = 8
    s := a[:]; t := s; t[1] = 9
    fmt.Println(a, b, s)
}

title: Methods, receivers and embedding
watch: Watch the `CopyTick` frame get its own copy of `c`, while the `Tick` frame holds an arrow back to `main`'s `c`.

title: Closures
watch: Watch the one `n` slot in `main`'s frame: whichever closure runs, it updates that same slot.

title: Interfaces
watch: Watch `value` in `main`'s frame: it records the type `*Item` even though the pointer inside it is nil.

title: Nil: one word, six meanings
watch: Notice `s` and `m` sit in `main`'s frame as nil, with no heap object behind them.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    var s []int
    var m map[string]int
    fmt.Println(len(s), len(m), m["missing"])
}

title: Errors
watch: Watch `cause` and `err` appear as two separate error values in `main`'s frame; `err` wraps `cause` rather than replacing it.

title: Defer, panic and recover
watch: Step to the end of `main`: nothing prints until `n` is already 2, then the deferred calls run newest first.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    n := 1
    defer fmt.Println("saved", n)
    defer func() { fmt.Println("latest", n) }()
    n = 2
}

title: Generics
watch: Watch two `Add` frames appear in turn: one where `a` and `b` are `int`, one where they are `int64`.

title: Stacks
watch: Watch `sum` frames pile up in the main goroutine's lane, each with a smaller `n`, then leave top-first as they return.

title: Escape analysis
watch: Watch `x` get marked as moved to the heap, and `p` in `main`'s frame keep its arrow to it after `makeValue`'s frame is gone.

title: Allocation
watch: Watch two heap objects appear for `a` and `b`, and check the size shown on each against the 13 and 33 bytes requested.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    a := make([]byte, 13)
    b := make([]byte, 33)
    fmt.Println(len(a), len(b))
}

title: Garbage collection basics
watch: Watch the global `keep` lose its arrow to the heap box, then see the GC mark phase skip that box and the sweep free it.

title: GC pacing and tuning
watch: Watch a 32-byte buffer appear on the heap each loop turn and lose its arrow when the turn ends, then see the GC sweep them.

title: Memory-friendly Go and leaks
watch: Watch `small`'s arrow point into the big 64-int array, while `copyOfSmall` points to its own 2-int array.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    large := make([]int, 64)
    small := large[:2]
    copyOfSmall := make([]int, len(small))
    copy(copyOfSmall, small)
    fmt.Println(len(small), cap(small), cap(copyOfSmall))
}

title: Goroutines
watch: Watch three new goroutine lanes open, each with its own `n`, while `main`'s lane waits at `wg.Wait()` until all three finish.

title: Creation
watch: Watch the new goroutine's lane appear with `value` already set to 7, before `main` changes `n` to 9.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ch := make(chan int)
    n := 7
    go func(value int) { ch <- value }(n)
    n = 9
    fmt.Println(<-ch, n)
}

title: The GMP scheduler
watch: Watch the goroutine lanes move between runnable, running and finished while the channel's buffer fills with 1 and 2.

title: Run queues and work stealing
watch: Watch new goroutines start as runnable and wait their turn; only one lane is running at any step.

title: Preemption
watch: Watch the worker's lane run its loop while `main`'s lane stays blocked on `<-done`, then wake when 190 arrives.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    done := make(chan int)
    go func(){ total := 0; for i := 0; i < 20; i++ { total += i }; done <- total }()
    fmt.Println(<-done)
}

title: Networking and the netpoller
watch: Watch the sleeping goroutine's lane park while the virtual clock moves, and `main` wait on `done` until 7 arrives.

title: Timers and sleeping
watch: Watch `main`'s lane park while the virtual clock jumps ahead 5 ms, then resume.

title: Channels
watch: Watch 3 and 5 sit in the channel's buffer and leave one per receive; after that, a receive gets 0 and `false`.
source:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ch := make(chan int, 2)
    ch <- 3; ch <- 5
    close(ch)
    a, ok := <-ch
    b := <-ch
    c, open := <-ch
    fmt.Println(a, ok, b, c, open)
}

title: Select
watch: Watch both channels hold one buffered value; `select` takes from only one of them, and the other value stays put.

title: Synchronization
watch: Watch only one goroutine lane hold the mutex at a time, while `main` stays blocked at `wg.Wait()`.

title: Ordering and the memory model
watch: Watch both goroutine lanes write `x` with no lock or channel between them, then look for the potential data race warning.

title: Pipelines
watch: Watch each value hop from `in` through the middle goroutine to `out`, and see each channel closed by the goroutine that sends on it.

title: Cancellation
watch: Watch the worker's lane sit blocked on `ctx.Done()`, then wake the moment `cancel()` closes it.

title: Concurrency bug clinic
watch: Watch `main` block at `wg.Wait()` until the worker's lane runs its deferred `wg.Done()`.

title: Diagnostics
watch: Watch one heap object appear for `data`, and compare its size with what `len` and `cap` print.

title: Profiling
watch: Watch a new 16-byte heap object appear on each loop turn while the previous one loses its arrow.

title: Tracing
watch: Watch `main`'s lane block on `<-ch` while the sender's lane runs, then see 4 cross the channel and `main` resume.
source:

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ch:=make(chan int)
    go func(){ch<-4}()
    fmt.Println(<-ch)
}
